# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Jan 4 - 10, 2026)

This week, the project made significant strides in preparing for a more interconnected Superchain by advancing cross-chain interoperability features. This forward-looking development was balanced by a deep focus on protocol stability, with major investigations into node behavior and critical bug fixes aimed at hardening the existing infrastructure.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Advancing Superchain Interoperability**
_Goal: To enable seamless communication and asset movement between chains in the Superchain, laying the groundwork for a unified ecosystem._
-   Core migration logic for cross-chain operations was implemented, providing a foundational piece for future interoperability features in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism).
-   The dispute game system was enhanced to allow claims to be retrieved across different L2 chains, a key requirement for cross-chain security in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism).
-   Work began to replace older components with the new `op-supernode`, a critical architectural shift that will support future interop capabilities in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism).

**Strengthening Protocol Stability and Security**
_Goal: To ensure the network remains robust, reliable, and secure, which is a top priority for protecting users and assets._
-   A deep, cross-team investigation was conducted to diagnose and propose fixes for Kona node instability related to L1 reorgs, a major effort to improve network resilience.
-   A critical bug that could cause the `op-batcher` component to crash was resolved, improving the stability of transaction processing in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism).
-   Protocol safety was enhanced by updating core specifications to mandate safer network parameters, starting with a non-zero elasticity value in [ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs).
-   The robustness of core smart contracts was improved by converting targeted tests into more comprehensive fuzz tests in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism).

**Expanding the Superchain Ecosystem**
_Goal: To grow the network of chains and available assets, which is key to increasing the utility and vibrancy of the Superchain._
-   Preparations began to onboard the new Karst L2 chain and enable its first network upgrade, signaling active growth of the Superchain in [ethereum-optimism/op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth).
-   The variety of assets available on Base and Celo was expanded by adding new tokens like DUAL, weETH, and wstETH to the official token list in [ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io).

**Improving Developer Experience and Documentation**
_Goal: To provide clear documentation and reliable tools that empower developers to build innovative applications on the OP Stack._
-   The configuration for chains in the Superchain was clarified by adding detailed documentation for the `SuperchainDefinition` type, resolving a long-standing ambiguity in [ethereum-optimism/specs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs).
-   A data integrity bug was fixed to ensure the reliability of analytics data, improving the quality of information available to developers and analysts in [ethereum-optimism/op-analytics](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics).
-   New documentation was proposed for governance processes and developer tooling, making it easier for the community to participate and build in [ethereum-optimism/docs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs).

### Cross-Repository Coordination

This week highlighted strong collaboration across multiple teams on several key initiatives:

-   **Kona Node Stability:** A major investigation into Kona node instability ([#18676](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/18676)) involved coordinated analysis across the `optimism`, `superchain-ops`, and `docs` repositories. This effort focused on a detailed root cause analysis of L2 reorgs, demonstrating a collective commitment to ensuring the stability of all node implementations.
-   **RPC Endpoint Correction:** A coordinated discussion took place across nearly all repositories to address a discrepancy in the `optimism_syncStatus` RPC endpoint ([#18673](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/18673)). Teams referenced shared design documents and specifications to align on a fix that maintains architectural consistency without introducing unnecessary complexity.
-   **Supernode Transition:** The strategic shift from `op-supervisor` to the new `op-supernode`
